entries.englishValueBefore: Bonds depend entirely on the government's ability and willingness to pay. If the government faces fiscal crisis, defaults, or decides to inflate away the debt, bondholders suffer.
entries.englishValue: Bonds depend entirely on governments paying back. If a government defaults or inflates away its debt, bondholders lose.
entries.currentValue: Àwọn ìfòwólé gbékẹ̀lé agbára àti ìfẹ́ ìkálẹ̀ láti san. Tí ìkálẹ̀ bá kójú àjàkálẹ̀ owó, kuna, tàbí pinnu láti fi owó ṣíṣé san gbèsè, àwọn oníní ìfòwólé yoo jìyà.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn ìfòwó-mu dá lórí ìjọba ńsanwó padà pátápátá. Bí ìjọba kan bá kùnà tàbí kó dín gbèsè rẹ̀ kù nípasẹ̀ owó-ṣíṣẹ́, àwọn olùní ìfòwó-mu pàdánù.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates independently of any government and cannot be controlled, inflated, or defaulted on by political authorities.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin operates independently of any government or political authority.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ lómìnìra kúrò nínú ìkálẹ̀ kaǹkaǹ a kò sì lè ṣàkoso ó, fi owó ṣíṣé bà à, tàbí kuna láti san nípà àwọn aláṣẹ oselu.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣiṣẹ́ lọ́tọ̀ kúrò lọ́wọ́ ìjọba kankan tàbí àṣẹ òṣèlú.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be sent anywhere in the world instantly over the Internet, while cash requires physical presence or trusted intermediaries. You can't email cash, but you can send Bitcoin to anyone with an Internet connection in minutes.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin moves over the internet anywhere in minutes. Cash needs physical presence or trusted couriers — you can't email a $20 bill.
entries.currentValue: A lè fi Bitcoin ranṣẹ́ sí ibìkìbì lágbàyé lẹ́sẹ̀kẹ̀sẹ̀ lórí Intaneti, lakoko tí owó ààmù nílò wíwà lárà tàbí alárinà tí a gbékẹ̀lé. O kò lè fi ìmèèlì fi owó ààmù, ṣùgbọ́n o lè fi Bitcoin ranṣẹ́ sí ẹ̀níkaǹkan tó ní àṣọsì Intaneti ní iṣẹ́jú díẹ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń lọ lórí ìntánẹ́ẹ̀tì níbi gbogbo láàárín ìṣẹ́jú díẹ̀. Owó ààmù nílò wíwà ní ti ara tàbí àwọn alámojúkùrò tí a gbẹ́kẹ̀lé — o kò lè fi ímeèlì rán owó dọ́là $20.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin works the same way everywhere in the world - there are no borders in the Bitcoin network. Cash is limited by geography, exchange rates, and local acceptance. Try using US dollars in rural Thailand or Japanese yen in rural Mexico.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin works the same way everywhere. Cash is limited by geography, exchange rates, and local acceptance.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ bákan náà ní ibìkìbì lágbàyé - kò sí àlà nínú nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì Bitcoin. Owó ààmù ní àlà àgbẹ̀gbẹ̀, iye pàṣípààrọ̀, àti gbígbà ag¹bègbè. Gbíyànjú láti lo dọ́là Amẹ́ríkà ní àwọn àgbẹ̀gbẹ̀ Thai tàbí yen Japáànù ní àgbẹ̀gbẹ̀ Mẹ́síkò.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣiṣẹ́ ní ọ̀nà kan náà níbi gbogbo. Owó ààmù ní ààlà nípasẹ̀ ilẹ̀, iye ìparí, àti ìtẹ́wọ́gbà àdúgbò.

entries.englishValueBefore: Governments can and do invalidate cash overnight through demonetization policies, like India did in 2016 when they banned certain banknotes.
entries.englishValue: Governments can invalidate cash overnight — India did it in 2016. Even without demonetization, cash loses value to
entries.currentValue: Àwọn ìkálẹ̀ lè, wọn sì máa ń, pa owó ààmù tì lórú nípà àwọn òfìn ìfowó-yìgaga, bíí India ti ṣe ní 2016 nígbà tí wọn fi ofìn de àwọn ìwé-owó kan.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn ìjọba lè ṣe owó ààmù ní aláìwúlò ní alẹ́ kan ṣoṣo — Indíà ṣe é ní 2016. Kódà láìní ìpa-iye, owó ààmù pàdánù iye sí

entries.englishValueBefore: Even without banning certain banknotes, governments constantly devalue cash through inflation.
entries.englishValue: inflation.
entries.currentValue: Pààpàà láì fi ofìn de àwọn ìwé-owó, àwọn ìkálẹ̀ máa ń din iye owó ààmù nígbàgbógbò nípà owó ṣíṣé.
entries.targetTranslation: owó-ṣíṣẹ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin cannot be invalidated by any government or authority - it exists on a global, decentralized network that no single entity controls.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin can't be invalidated by any government or authority.
entries.currentValue: A kò lè pa Bitcoin tì nípà ìkálẹ̀ tàbí aláṣẹ kaǹkaǹ - ó wà lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì aláìpín-ààrìn lágbàyé tí ẹ̀da kanṣoṣo kò lè ṣàkoso.
entries.targetTranslation: Kò sí ìjọba tàbí àṣẹ tí ó lè sọ Bitcoin di aláìwúlò.

entries.englishValueBefore: Cash can be counterfeited, and it's often difficult to detect fake bills without special equipment. Even with security features, counterfeit cash continues to circulate. Bitcoin uses cryptographic proof that makes counterfeiting mathematically impossible.
entries.englishValue: Cash can be counterfeited, sometimes convincingly. Bitcoin uses cryptography that makes counterfeiting mathematically impossible.
entries.currentValue: A lè dá èké owó ààmù, ó sì máa ń ṣòro láti mọ̀ àwọn ìwé-owó ìró láì ní èrọ pàtàkì. Pààpàà pẹ̀lú àwọn èṣò ààbò, èké owó ààmù ṣì ń kààkìrí. Bitcoin lo èrí cryptographic tó jẹ́ kí dídá èké rẹ̀ jẹ́ aìléṣe ní mathematics.
entries.targetTranslation: A lè kọ owó ààmù dáni tàbí lè ṣe é ní àwòkọ, nígbà mìíràn ní ọ̀nà tí ó dájú. Bitcoin lo cryptography tí ó sọ àwòkọ di aláìṣeéṣe ní ọ̀nà ìṣirò.

entries.englishValueBefore: Cash is issued and controlled by governments, who can print more at will, change designs, or declare certain bills invalid. Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network where no single authority has control over the money supply or rules.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no central authority. Cash is issued by governments that can print more, change designs, or invalidate notes at will.
entries.currentValue: Àwọn ìkálẹ̀ ni ó máa ń ṣàjàdé àti ṣàkoso owó ààmù, wọn lè tẹ̀ díẹ̀ síì nígbà tí wọn bá fẹ́, yí àpẹẹrẹ padà, tàbí kèdè pé àwọn ìwé-owó kan kò wúlò mọ́. Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì aláìpín-ààrìn tí aláṣẹ kanṣoṣo kò lè ṣàkoso ìpese owó tàbí àwọn ofìn.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò ní àṣẹ àárín. Àwọn ìjọba ń tẹ̀ owó ààmù tí wọ́n lè tẹ̀ síi, yí àpẹẹrẹ rẹ̀ padà, tàbí kí wọ́n sọ ọ́ di aláìwúlò ní àkókò tí wọ́n bá fẹ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Cash must be stored physically, making it vulnerable to theft, loss, fire, or confiscation. Large amounts require expensive security measures.
entries.englishValue: Cash is vulnerable to theft, fire, loss, and confiscation. Bitcoin can be securely
entries.currentValue: A gbọ̀dọ̀ pamó́ owó ààmù lárà, èyí tó mú kí ó wà ní ewu olè, pàdánú, iná, tàbí gbage. Àwọn iye owó nlá nílò ààbò olówó.
entries.targetTranslation: Owó ààmù lè jẹ́ jíjí, jíjóná, sísọnù, àti ìgbà-pa. Bitcoin lè wà ní ààbò pẹ̀lú

entries.englishValueBefore: But Bitcoin can be securely stored in self-custody
entries.englishValue: self-custodied
entries.currentValue: Ṣùgbọ́n a lè pamó́ Bitcoin ní ààbò nínú ìṣàkoso-arà
entries.targetTranslation: ìṣàkóso-ara

entries.englishValueBefore: using a smartphone app or specialized wallet, giving you complete control over your money without physical storage risks.
entries.englishValue: on a phone or hardware device.
entries.currentValue: nípà lílò àpù fóónù alagbékà tàbí àpò owó pàtàkì, èyí tó fún ọ ní àṣẹ kikun lórí owó rẹ láì ní ewu ìpàmó́ lárà.
entries.targetTranslation: lórí ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ tàbí ohun-èlò amúnaláti.

entries.englishValueBefore: Cash has minimum denominations - you can't split a penny into smaller parts. Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, enabling micropayments and precise transactions of any amount.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats, enabling micropayments of any size. Cash has minimum denominations — you can't split a penny.
entries.currentValue: Owó ààmù ní ìṣè̀lẹ̀ - o kò lè pín senti sí apá kékeré. A lè pín Bitcoin sí èké kékeré miliọ́nù 100 tí a ń pè ní satoshis, tó mú kí a lè ṣe àwọn ìsàn owó kékeré púpọ̀ àti iṣòwò tó pé ní iye kaǹkaǹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin pin sí 100 mílíọ̀nù sats, tí ó ṣe àwọn ìsanwó kéré-kéré ti ìwọ̀n èyíkéyìí. Owó ààmù ní àwọn iye tí ó kéré jùlọ — o kò lè pin pení kan.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is the most secure computing network that has ever existed and has never been hacked. CBDCs rely on governments and banks to secure the network, which have been hacked countless times throughout history.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is the most secure computing network ever built and has never been hacked. CBDCs rely on banks and governments that have been hacked countless times.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì kọ̀mpútà tó ààbò jùlọ tí ó tíì wà rí àti pé a kò tíì hack à. Àwọn CBDC gbékẹ̀lé àwọn ìkálẹ̀ àti àwọn ilé-ìfòwópàmó́ láti ṣe ààbò nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì, èyí tí a ti hack ní ìgbà púpọ̀ nínú ìtàn.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ni nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì ìṣirò tí ó ní ààbò jùlọ tí a tíì kọ́, ó sì kò tíì jẹ́ kí a ja jó. Àwọn CBDC dá lórí àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ àti ìjọba tí a ti jagunjagun lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is designed to give you total control over your money.
entries.englishValue: Nobody can stop you from transacting with Bitcoin. CBDCs are designed so governments and central banks can control every payment, limiting your privacy and freedom.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ti ṣẹ̀dá láti fun ọ ní àṣẹ kikun lórí owó rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Kò sí ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó lè dí ọ lọ́wọ́ ìṣòwò pẹ̀lú Bitcoin. A kọ́ àwọn CBDC kí ìjọba àti àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ àárín lè darí gbogbo ìsanwó, èyí ń díwọ̀n àdáni àti òmìnira rẹ.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin never expires and has no monthly fees.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin never expires and has no monthly fees. CBDCs can be programmed to expire, preventing you from saving for the future.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin kò parí láéláé kò sì ní owó ìsàn oṣoọ̀ṣè.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò ní akọsílẹ̀ ìparí, kò sì ní owó oṣù. Àwọn CBDC lè jẹ́ kí o pari, èyí ń dí ọ lọ́wọ́ láti pa owó mọ́ fún ọjọ́ iwájú.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC that will ever exist.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC. CBDCs have no cap on supply, allowing governments to expand money at will — which causes
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní opin lílé ti miliọ́nù 21 BTC tí yoo wà láéláé.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ní ààlà tó dúró tí 21 mílíọ̀nù BTC. Àwọn CBDC kò ní ààlà lórí ìpèsè, èyí ń jẹ́ kí ìjọba lè fẹ̀ owó ní àkókò tí wọ́n fẹ́ — èyí tí ó ń fa

entries.englishValueBefore: CBDCs, much like the government currencies we use today, have no cap on total supply. This lack of cap on total supply allows the government to expand the money supply.
entries.englishValue: inflation.
entries.currentValue: Àwọn CBDC, bíí àwọn owó ìkálẹ̀ wa lónìí, kò ní opin ìpese. Àìní opin ìpese yìí gba ìkálẹ̀ láàyè láti fi owó ṣíṣé bà ìpese owó.
entries.targetTranslation: owó-ṣíṣẹ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin addresses are pseudonymous, which means they are not linked to your real name or identity. CBDCs are directly linked to your real name and identity which enables massive financial surveillance and censorship.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin addresses aren't tied to your real identity. CBDCs link directly to government ID, enabling mass financial surveillance and censorship.
entries.currentValue: Àwọn àdírẹ́ṣì Bitcoin jẹ́ orukọ ì̀kòkò, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé wọn kò so mó́ orukọ gídi rẹ tàbí ìdanimò rẹ. Àwọn CBDC so tààrà mó́ orukọ gídi rẹ àti ìdanimò rẹ èyí tó mú kí àbòjútó owó àti ìṣàkoso nlá ṣèṣè.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn àdírẹ́sì Bitcoin kò ní ìsopọ̀ pẹ̀lú orúkọ gidi rẹ. Àwọn CBDC ní ìsopọ̀ tààrà pẹ̀lú ID ìjọba, èyí ń ṣe àkíyèsí àti ìfagilé ti owó ní àpapọ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: The Bitcoin network is decentralized.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's rules are validated by tens of thousands of independent nodes. CBDCs are centralized in government and central-bank hands, which hold complete control over the network.
entries.currentValue: Nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì Bitcoin jẹ́ aláìpín-ààrìn.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn ìlànà Bitcoin ni a ń jẹ́rìí sí nípasẹ̀ ẹgbẹẹgbẹ̀rún àwọn nodes òmìnira. Àwọn CBDC ti darí ní àárín ní ọwọ́ ìjọba àti ilé-ìfowópamọ́ àárín, tí ó ní agbára pípé lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin allows anyone to run a node that verifies the rules of the network are being followed. CBDCs don't allow anyone to run nodes and rely on trust in the government and central banks.
entries.englishValue: Anyone can run a Bitcoin node to verify the rules of the network. CBDCs don't allow users to run nodes — you have to trust the central authority.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin gba ẹ̀níkaǹkan láàyè láti ṣíṣè ógó̀ tó ṣàyẹ̀wò pé àwọn ofìn nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì náà tèlé. Àwọn CBDC kò gba ẹ̀níkaǹkan láàyè láti ṣíṣè ógó̀ ó sì gbékẹ̀lé ìgbékẹ̀lé nínú ìkálẹ̀ àti àwọn ilé-ìfòwópàmó́ ààrìn.
entries.targetTranslation: Ẹnikẹ́ni lè ṣiṣẹ́ Bitcoin node láti jẹ́rìí àwọn ìlànà nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì. Àwọn CBDC kò gbà fún àwọn olùmúlò láti ṣiṣẹ́ nodes — o ní láti gbẹ́kẹ̀lé àṣẹ àárín.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is designed to make it impossible for others to freeze your money. CBDCs are designed to make it easy for governments and central banks to freeze your money.
entries.englishValue: Self-custodied Bitcoin can't be frozen by anyone. CBDCs are designed so governments and central banks can freeze accounts instantly.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ti ṣẹ̀dá láti mú kí ó jẹ́ aìlẹ́ṣe fún àwọn ẹ̀lòmìràn láti dí owó rẹ. Àwọn CBDC ti ṣẹ̀dá láti mú kí ó rọ̀rùn fún àwọn ìkálẹ̀ àti àwọn ilé-ìfòwópàmó́ ààrìn láti dí owó rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: A kò lè dí Bitcoin tí ó wà ní ìṣàkóso-ara lọ́wọ́ ẹnikẹ́ni. A kọ́ àwọn CBDC kí ìjọba àti ilé-ìfowópamọ́ àárín lè dí àpótí lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is designed to give you full control over your money.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin gives you full control over your money when you self-custody it with a
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ti ṣẹ̀dá láti fun ọ ní àṣẹ kikun lórí owó rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin fún ọ ní agbára pípé lórí owó rẹ nígbà tí o bá ṣe ìṣàkóso-ara pẹ̀lú

entries.englishValueBefore: Just make sure you withdraw it to a self-custody wallet.
entries.englishValue: wallet.
entries.currentValue: Kàn rí dájú pé o yọ̀ ó kúrò sí àpò owó ìṣàkoso-arà.
entries.targetTranslation: àpò.

entries.englishValueBefore: When you self-custody your bitcoin, no one can stop you from accessing your money.
entries.englishValue: CBDCs require trusting custodians like banks or governments to hold your money for you.
entries.currentValue: Nígbà tí o bá ṣe ìṣàkoso-arà bitcoin rẹ, kò sí ẹ̀níkan tó lè da ọ́ dúró láti ní iràyè sí owó rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn CBDC nílò ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé sí àwọn olùdúró bí àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ tàbí ìjọba láti dúró pẹ̀lú owó rẹ.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a predictable monetary policy that is fixed in code and can't be changed. CBDCs, like our currencies today, have a monetary policy that can easily be changed.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's monetary policy is fixed in code and can't be changed. CBDCs can be reprogrammed at will by politicians, causing
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní ìlànà owó tó hàn tó wà tèlẹ̀ nínú koodu tí a kò lè yí padà. Àwọn CBDC, bíí àwọn owó wa lónìí, ní ìlànà owó tí a lè yí padà ní ìrọ̀rùn.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìlànà owó Bitcoin ti múlẹ̀ ní koodu, kò sì lè yípadà. A lè tún àwọn CBDC ṣe láìpẹ́ nípa àwọn olóṣèlú, èyí ń fa

entries.englishValueBefore: This results in inflation when politicians print too much money.
entries.englishValue: inflation
entries.currentValue: Èyí máa ń fa owó ṣíṣé nígbà tí àwọn oloselu bá tẹ̀ owó púpọ̀ jù.
entries.targetTranslation: owó-ṣíṣẹ́

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin's protocol has remained fundamentally unchanged since 2009, providing predictable rules that cannot be easily altered. Most crypto projects frequently update their protocols, change tokenomics, or fork into new versions, creating uncertainty for users.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's protocol has stayed fundamentally the same since 2009, providing predictable rules. Most crypto projects constantly change protocols, tokenomics, or fork into new versions.
entries.currentValue: Ètò Bitcoin ti wà láì yípadà látì 2009, tó máa ń pèṣè àwọn ofìn tó hàn tí a kò lè yí padà ní ìrọ̀rùn. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto máa ń ṣàjú ètò wọn nígbàgbígbà, yípadà tokenomics, tàbí pín sí àwọn ẹ̀yà tuntun, tó máa ń ṣẹ̀dá àì dájú fún àwọn olùmúlò.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìlànà Bitcoin ti dúró bákan náà látinú ọdún 2009, ó ń pèsè àwọn ìlànà tí a lè sọ àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ rẹ̀. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣẹ̀dá crypto ń yí àwọn ìlànà, tokenomics, tàbí kí wọ́n pín sí àwọn ẹ̀dà tuntun léraléra.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a truly decentralized network with tens of thousands of independent nodes worldwide. Many crypto projects are controlled by foundations, companies, or small groups of developers who can make unilateral decisions about the protocol's future.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin runs on tens of thousands of independent nodes worldwide. Most crypto projects are controlled by foundations, companies, or small dev teams that can make unilateral changes.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì aláìpín-ààrìn òtítọ́ pẹ̀lú ẹgèbẹrún àwọn ógó̀ òmìnìra lágbàyé. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto ni àwọn ìgbìmọ̀, àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́, tàbí àwọn ègbẹ́ kékeré àwọn olupìlẹ̀ṣẹ̀ tó lè ṣe àwọn ìpinnu aláìpín-ààrìn nípa ọ̀là ètò náà ń ṣàkoso.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí ẹgbẹẹgbẹ̀rún àwọn nodes òmìnira ní àgbáyé. Àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣẹ̀dá crypto ọ̀pọ̀ jùlọ ni a ti darí nípasẹ̀ àwọn ipilẹ̀ṣẹ̀, ilé-iṣẹ́, tàbí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ olùgbé kéré tí wọ́n lè ṣe àwọn ìyípadà fúnra wọn.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million coins that will ever exist, making it the scarcest digital asset. Most crypto projects have unlimited supplies, inflationary mechanisms, or can mint new tokens at will, diluting holder value over time.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million coins — the scarcest digital asset. Most crypto projects have unlimited supplies or mechanisms to mint new tokens at will, diluting holders.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní opin lílé ti miliọ́nù 21 owó tí yoo wà láéláé, tó mú kí ó jẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ oni-nọ́míbà tó ṣòwọ́n jùlọ. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto ní ìpese aìlópin, ètò owó ṣíṣé, tàbí lè tẹ̀ àwọn token tuntun nígbà tí wọn bá fẹ́, tó máa ń din iye oníní kù.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ní ààlà tó dúró tí 21 mílíọ̀nù coin — ohun ìní oníyebíye dígítà tí ó kéré jùlọ. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣẹ̀dá crypto ní ìpèsè aláìlópin tàbí ọ̀nà láti dá àwọn token tuntun ní àkókò tí wọ́n fẹ́, èyí ń dín àwọn olùní kù.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has one simple purpose: peer-to-peer digital money. Anyone can understand and use it with basic knowledge. Many crypto projects involve complex smart contracts, DeFi protocols, or governance mechanisms that require technical expertise to use safely.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has one purpose: peer-to-peer digital money. Anyone can understand and use it. Most crypto involves complex smart contracts or DeFi that require technical expertise to use safely.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní àfàànì kanṣoṣo: owó oni-nọ́míbà ẹ̀nìyàn-sí-ẹ̀nìyàn. Ẹ̀níkaǹkan lè lóyé àti lò pẹ̀lú ìmọ̀ ìpìlẹ̀. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto kan àwọn àdéhùn smart contract, ètò DeFi, tàbí ètò ìṣàkoso tó nílò ìmọ̀ imọ̀-ẹ̀rọ̀ láti lò ní ààbò.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ní ète kan ṣoṣo: owó dígítà ẹnikẹ́ni-sí-ẹnikẹ́ni. Ẹnikẹ́ni lè lóye ó sì lò ó. Ọ̀pọ̀ crypto ní àwọn smart contract díjú tàbí DeFi tí ó nílò ìmọ̀-ìmọ̀ ọnà láti lò ní àìséwu.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin uses Proof of Work consensus, which has been battle-tested for over 15 years without a single successful attack on the main network. Many crypto projects use experimental consensus mechanisms like Proof of Stake or delegated systems that haven't proven their long-term security.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's Proof of Work has run without a successful attack on the main network for over 15 years. Most crypto projects use experimental consensus that hasn't been battle-tested.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin lò ìgbàgbọ́ Proof of Work, èyí tí a ti dánwò ní ogun fún ọ̀dún 15 jù láì ní ìkọ̀lù kan lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì àkó̀kó̀. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto lo àwọn ètò ìgbàgbọ́ àdánìwò bíí Proof of Stake tí kò tíì fi hàn ààbò ìgbà pipẹ́.
entries.targetTranslation: Proof of Work Bitcoin ti ń ṣiṣẹ́ láìsí ìkọlù tí ó ṣàṣeyọrí lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì pàtàkì fún ó ju ọdún 15. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣẹ̀dá crypto ń lo ètò àdéhùn àdánwò tí a kò tí ìdánwò ní ogun.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin serves as digital money - a store of value and medium of exchange. Most crypto tokens are utility tokens for specific platforms, governance tokens, or speculative assets with unclear real-world value propositions.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is digital money — a store of value and medium of exchange. Most crypto tokens are speculative utility or governance tokens with unclear real-world value.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ gégé bí owó oni-nọ́míbà - àfi-pamó́ iye àti ìlò pàṣípààrọ̀. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn crypto token jẹ́ token ìlò fún àwọn pèpè kan pàtó, token ìṣàkoso, tàbí ọ̀rọ̀ amàṣẹ pẹ̀lú ànfààní iye àgbáyé gídi tó kò hàn.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ owó dígítà — ìfowópamọ́ iye àti ohun-èlò ìparí. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn token crypto jẹ́ àwọn token oníṣẹ́ tàbí ìjọba ipò ìparowó pẹ̀lú iye gidi-aiyé tí kò ṣe kedere.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin becomes stronger under attack and has survived every crisis, ban, and criticism thrown at it. Most crypto projects are fragile and can collapse from regulatory pressure, technical failures, or market downturns.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin grows stronger under attack and has survived every crisis, ban, and criticism. Most crypto projects collapse under regulatory, technical, or market pressure.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń lagbara síì lábé̀ ìkọ̀lù àti pé ó ti yè gbogbo àjàkálẹ̀, fífi ofìn de, àti àtàkò tí a fi sí. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto jẹ́ aláìtàn tí wọn lè wó láti titipa ofìn, ikùna imọ̀-ẹ̀rọ̀, tàbí ìdìnkù ọ̀jà.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń di alágbára síi nínú ìkọlù, ó sì ti là gbogbo àjálù, ìfòfindè, àti àríwísí kọjá. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣẹ̀dá crypto ń ṣubú nínú ìfagilé ìlànà, ìmọ̀-ìmọ̀ ọnà, tàbí ìfagilé ọjà.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has no CEO, no company behind it, and no single point of failure. Many crypto projects are backed by venture capital firms, have identifiable leadership teams, or depend on specific companies for their continued operation.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no CEO, no company, no single point of failure. Most crypto projects depend on VCs, specific leadership, or one company's survival.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin kò ní CEO, kò ní ilé-iṣẹ́ léyìn rẹ̀, kò sì ní ibì kiko kanṣoṣo. Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́ àkànṣe crypto ní atilẹ́yìn láti àwọn ile-iṣẹ́ venture capital, ní àwọn ègbẹ́ aláṣẹ tó hàn, tàbí gbékẹ̀lé àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ pàtó fún iṣẹ́ wọn láti tẹ̀síwájú.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò ní CEO, kò ní ilé-iṣẹ́, kò ní ojú-ìkùnà kan. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣẹ̀dá crypto dá lórí àwọn VC, àwọn olórí pàtó, tàbí ìwà-ìpè ilé-iṣẹ́ kan.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is perfectly fungible, meaning every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable - one bitcoin equals one bitcoin anywhere in the world. Fine art is non-fungible by nature, with each piece being unique in its creation, history, condition, and provenance, making direct comparisons and valuations extremely difficult.
entries.englishValue: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable. Every artwork is unique — different creation, history, condition, and provenance make direct comparisons extremely difficult.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ alápàrò dáadáa, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé bitcoin kọ̀ọ̀kan dabi arà wọn àti pé a lè pàṣípààrọ̀ wọn - bitcoin kan dọ́gba bitcoin kan ní ibìkìbì lágbáyé. Awò̀ràn giga jẹ́ aláì-pàrò láti ibì-àyé, kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ aláìlẹ́gbẹ́ nínú ìlọ̀dá, ìtàn, ipo, àti ìpìlẹ̀ṣẹ̀, tó mú kí àfiwé tààrà àti idiyèlé ṣòro púpọ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ bákan náà ó sì lè rọ́pò. Iṣẹ́ ọnà kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ aláìṣe-bákan-náà — ìṣẹ̀dá tó yàtọ̀, ìtàn, ipò, àti orísun jẹ́ kí ìfiwéra tààrà ṣòro gan-an.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin trades on a global 24/7 market where anyone with internet access can buy or sell instantly. Fine art requires specialized auction houses like Sotheby's or Christie's, private dealers, or exclusive galleries. Sales can take months to arrange and complete, with limited market access and irregular trading opportunities.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin trades 24/7 on a global market accessible to anyone. Fine art requires specialized auction houses, private dealers, or galleries and can take months to sell.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ń ṣòwò lórí ọ̀jà àgbáyé 24/7 tí ẹ̀níkaǹkan tó ní iràyè intaneti lè ra tàbí ta lẹ́sẹ̀kẹ̀sẹ̀. Awò̀ràn giga nílò àwọn ilé titaja pàtàkì bíí Sotheby's tàbí Christie's, àwọn olùtà àdání, tàbí àwọn ilé-àṣà pàtàkì. Títà lè gba oṣù láti ṣetò àti parí.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣòwò 24/7 lórí ọjà àgbáyé tí ẹnikẹ́ni lè rí. Iṣẹ́ ọnà giga nílò àwọn ilé-ìpolówó pàtó, àwọn alágbàta àdáni, tàbí àwọn gallery ó sì lè gba oṣù láti tà.

entries.englishValueBefore: Buying or selling bitcoin typically costs less than 1% in fees, often much less. Fine art sales involve substantial costs including buyer's premiums (10-25%), seller's commissions (10-15%), insurance, transportation, storage, and authentication fees. These combined costs can easily exceed 30-40% of the artwork's value in a single transaction.
entries.englishValue: Buying or selling Bitcoin costs under 1% in fees, often much less. Art sales rack up 30–40% in buyer's premiums, commissions, insurance, transport, and authentication fees.
entries.currentValue: Rírà tàbí títà bitcoin máa ń jẹ́ kéré jù 1% ní owó ìsàn. Títà awò̀ràn giga kan àwọn ínàowó nlá pẹ̀lú àwọn owó olurà (10-25%), kọ́míṣọ́nù olutà (10-15%), ìrànsí, gbigbe, ìpàmó́, àti owó ìṣẹ́dájú. Àwọn ínàowó wọ̀nyí lè ju 30-40% iye awò̀ràn náà lọ.
entries.targetTranslation: Rírà tàbí títà Bitcoin ná kéré sí 1% nínú àwọn owó, sábà jẹ́ kéré jùlọ. Títà iṣẹ́ ọnà kó 30–40% nínú àwọn owó-rírà, owó-ìṣẹ̀, ìdánilójú, àkójọpọ̀, àti àyẹ̀wò òdodo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, making it perfect for transactions of any size from microtransactions to large purchases. Fine art cannot be divided - you cannot own a fraction of a painting or sell just part of a sculpture. This indivisibility limits investment flexibility and liquidity options.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats, making it perfect for any size transaction. You can't own a fraction of a painting or a corner of a sculpture without counterparty risk.
entries.currentValue: A lè pín Bitcoin sí èké kékeré miliọ́nù 100 tí a ń pè ní satoshis, tó dara fún iṣòwò ìwọn kaǹkaǹ láti kékeré sí nlá. A kò lè pín awò̀ràn giga - o kò lè ní apá kan awò̀ràn tàbí ta apá kan èrè òkútà.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin pín sí 100 mílíọ̀nù sats, èyí jẹ́ kí ó pé fún ìṣòwò ti ìwọ̀n èyíkéyìí. O kò lè ní apá kan iṣẹ́ ọnà tàbí ọ̀kan-ká àwòrán laìní ewu alábàárìn.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin ownership and authenticity can be cryptographically verified on the blockchain by anyone with basic technical knowledge. Fine art requires expensive expert authentication, provenance research, and scientific analysis. Even with expert verification, forgeries regularly fool the art world, and authentication disputes can destroy an artwork's value overnight. Bitcoin, on the other hand, cannot be forged or counterfeited.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin ownership and authenticity can be cryptographically verified by anyone on-chain. Art authentication is expensive, slow, and still routinely fooled by forgers — destroying an artwork's value overnight.
entries.currentValue: Níní Bitcoin àti òtítọ́ rẹ̀ lè jẹ́ ṣàyẹ̀wò lórí blockchain nípà ẹ̀níkaǹkan tó ní ìmọ̀ imọ̀-ẹ̀rọ̀ ìpìlẹ̀. Awò̀ràn giga nílò ìṣẹ́dájú ogbòn olówó, ìwádìí ìpìlẹ̀ṣẹ̀, àti àtúpàlẹ̀ ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ̀. Pààpàà pẹ̀lú ìṣẹ́dájú ogbòn, èké máa ń tan àgbáyé awò̀ràn lórèèkórèè. A kò sì lè dá èké Bitcoin.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìní àti òdodo Bitcoin ni a lè jẹ́rìí sí ní ọ̀nà cryptographic nípasẹ̀ ẹnikẹ́ni lórí blockchain. Àyẹ̀wò òdodo ọnà ná, ó lọ́ra, àwọn aláyàwòran ń tan ún sí ní ìgbà gbogbo — èyí ń pa iye iṣẹ́ ọnà run ní alẹ́ kan.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin, when backed up properly, cannot be destroyed by floods, fires, earthquakes, hurricanes, theft, or other disasters. Fine art is vulnerable to all forms of physical destruction and deterioration. Even with expensive climate-controlled storage and comprehensive insurance, artworks can be damaged by environmental factors, accidents, or natural disasters, potentially losing all value.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin, backed up properly, survives floods, fires, earthquakes, and theft. Fine art is vulnerable to every form of physical destruction, and insurance rarely covers it all.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin, tí a bá ṣe àfiípamó́ rẹ̀ dáadáa, a kò lè pa run nípà ìkunomi, iná, ìlù, ìjikoko, olè, tàbí àwọn àjálù mìràn. Awò̀ràn giga wà ní ewu gbogbo irú ìpa run lárà àti ìdíbàjẹ́.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin, tí a bá ti dáàbò bo dáadáa, ó là ìkún omi, iná, ìmìtìtì ilẹ̀, àti olè kọjá. Iṣẹ́ ọnà giga jẹ́ aláìlágbára sí gbogbo ọ̀nà ìparun ti ara, ìdánilójú sì sábà ò ní ní bo gbogbo rẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be bought and sold by anyone with internet access and a small amount of money to invest. Fine art investment is largely limited to wealthy collectors due to high minimum prices, exclusive auction access, storage requirements, insurance costs, and the specialized knowledge needed to navigate the art market successfully.
entries.englishValue: Anyone with an internet connection and a little money can buy Bitcoin. Fine art investment is effectively limited to wealthy collectors with auction access and specialized knowledge.
entries.currentValue: Enikaǹkan tó ní iràyè intaneti àti iye owó kékeré láti doko lè ra àti ta Bitcoin. Idókò awò̀ràn giga jẹ́ fun àwọn olórò nikan nitórí iye owó tó ga, iràyè titaja pàtàkì, ohun-èlò ìpàmó́, owó ìsàn ìrànsí, àti ìmọ̀ amó̀jú tí a nílò láti lò ọ̀jà awò̀ràn dáadáa.
entries.targetTranslation: Ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó ní ìsopọ̀ ìntánẹ́ẹ̀tì àti owó díẹ̀ lè ra Bitcoin. Ìnáwó iṣẹ́ ọnà giga ní ààlà sí àwọn olówó tí ó lè wọ àwọn ìpolówó pẹ̀lú ìmọ̀ pàtó.

entries.englishValueBefore: Because Bitcoin is digital, it can be sent almost instantly for very low fees by anyone with an Internet connection. Because Gold is physical, it cannot be moved across the Internet and must be physically shipped to transfer ownership.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin can be sent instantly over the internet for low fees. Gold must be physically shipped to transfer ownership.
entries.currentValue: Nítórí pé Bitcoin jẹ́ oni-nọ́míbà, a lè fi ranṣẹ́ lẹ́sẹ̀kẹ̀sẹ̀ pẹ̀lú owó ìsàn kékeré nípà ẹ̀níkaǹkan tó ní àṣọsì Intaneti. Nítórí pé Goolu jẹ́ tárà, a kò lè gbé è kọ̀já lórí Intaneti a sì gbọ̀dọ̀ fi í ranṣẹ́ lárà láti yí níní padà.
entries.targetTranslation: A lè rán Bitcoin lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀ lórí ìntánẹ́ẹ̀tì pẹ̀lú owó kéré. Goolu ní láti firànṣẹ́ ní ti ara láti gbé ìní gba.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is a digitally native asset, which means you can transfer full ownership of it over the Internet. Some companies offer the ability to buy gold online without receiving the actual physical gold, instead trusting the company to hold the gold for you. This is more like a Digital IOU since you only own a promise from the company instead of the actual asset.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is a digitally native asset you can transfer over the internet. Online gold is a Digital IOU — you only own a promise from a custodian, not the metal itself.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ oni-nọ́míbà láti ibì-àyé, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé o lè yí níní kikun rẹ̀ padà lórí Intaneti. Àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ kan pèṣè ànfààní rà goolu lórí aíyélújárà láì gba goolu lárà gan-an, dípo kí o gbékẹ̀lé ilé-iṣẹ́ náà láti tójú goolu náà fún ọ. Èyí dàbí IOU Oni-nọ́míbà nítórí pé o ní ìlérí láti ọ̀dọ̀ ilé-iṣẹ́ níkan dípò ọ̀rọ̀ gan-an.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ ohun-ìní dígítà-bíbí tí o lè gbé lórí ìntánẹ́ẹ̀tì. Goolu lórí ìntánẹ́ẹ̀tì jẹ́ IOU dígítà — o ní ìlérí lọ́wọ́ olùdúró nìkan, kì í ṣe irin náà fúnra rẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 Million BTC that will ever exist.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC. Gold's supply grows about 1.6% per year, shrinking your slice — less than fiat
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní opin lílé ti Miliọ́nù 21 BTC tí yoo wà láéláé.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ní ààlà tó dúró tí 21 mílíọ̀nù BTC. Ìpèsè goolu ń pọ̀ sí nípa 1.6% ní ọdún kan, èyí ń dín apá rẹ kù — kéré sí

entries.englishValueBefore: New gold supply is pulled out of the ground each year, resulting in inflation of the total supply. It's estimated that the total supply of gold increases by about 1.6% per year, which means your slice of the pie shrinks by 1.6% per year.
entries.englishValue: inflation
entries.currentValue: Ìpese goolu tuntun máa ń jáde lábé̀ ilẹ̀ lóọ̀dún, èyí máa ń fa owó ṣíṣé sí ìpese lápàpọ̀. A ṣe iro pé ìpese goolu lápàpọ̀ máa ń pọ̀ sí ní 1.6% lóọ̀dún, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé apá rẹ nínú akàrà máa ń din kù ní 1.6% lóọ̀dún.
entries.targetTranslation: owó-ṣíṣẹ́

entries.englishValueBefore: This is less than fiat inflation, but still inflation.
entries.englishValue: — but still inflation.
entries.currentValue: Èyí kéré jù owó ṣíṣé fiat, ṣùgbọ́n ó ṣì jẹ́ owó ṣíṣé.
entries.targetTranslation: fiat — ṣùgbọ́n òùnń jẹ́ owó-ṣíṣẹ́ síi.

entries.englishValueBefore: Gold has an elastic supply, meaning that as the price of gold rises, there is a greater incentive to mine more gold. This often puts downward pressure on the gold price as new mines come online.
entries.englishValue: When gold prices rise, more gold gets mined, pushing the price back down. Bitcoin's supply is inelastic — no matter how high the price goes, there will only ever be 21 million.
entries.currentValue: Goolu ní ìpese rírọ̀, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé bí iye goolu ṣe ń ga, ìjiyàn díẹ̀ síì ni wà láti wa goolu díẹ̀ síì. Èyí máa ń fa iye goolu sílẹ̀ nígbà tí àwọn ibì iwakusa tuntun bá bẹ̀rẹ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Nígbà tí iye goolu bá pọ̀ sí, a ó wa goolu síi, èyí yóò sì tì iye padà sí ìsàlẹ̀. Ìpèsè Bitcoin kò yí — láìbi-kojá iye náà ti ga tó, 21 mílíọ̀nù nìkan ni yóò máa wà títí láé.

entries.englishValueBefore: The Bitcoin network is decentralized.
entries.englishValue: Tens of thousands of independent nodes validate the Bitcoin network. Most physical gold sits in a handful of large custodian vaults.
entries.currentValue: Nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì Bitcoin jẹ́ aláìpín-ààrìn.
entries.targetTranslation: Ẹgbẹẹgbẹ̀rún àwọn nodes òmìnira ń jẹ́rìí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì Bitcoin. Ọ̀pọ̀ goolu ti ara wà ní ọwọ́ àwọn olùdúró ńlá díẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: With Bitcoin, it's incredibly easy to verify that you have real Bitcoin by taking self-custody of your coins and running a full node.
entries.englishValue: Anyone can verify real Bitcoin by running a full node — it's just an app. Verifying physical gold requires melting it down; the inside could be tungsten.
entries.currentValue: Pẹ̀lú Bitcoin, ó rọ̀rùn gán láti ṣàyẹ̀wò pé o ní Bitcoin òtítọ́ nípà gbígbà ìṣàkoso-arà àwọn owó rẹ àti ṣíṣẹ ógó̀ kikun.
entries.targetTranslation: Ẹnikẹ́ni lè jẹ́rìí Bitcoin gidi nípa ṣíṣiṣẹ́ node ní kíkún — ó kàn jẹ́ app. Jíjẹ́rìí goolu ti ara nílò sísún ún sí omi; tungsten lè wà nínú.

entries.englishValueBefore: Just like there are 100 cents in 1 dollar, there are 100,000,000 sats in 1 Bitcoin. This enables Bitcoin to be used for all scales of purchases, including microtransactions as small as a few cents.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats, making it perfect for any size purchase. Gold can't be easily divided for small transactions.
entries.currentValue: Gégé bí senti 100 ṣe wà nínú dọ́là 1, sats 100,000,000 wà nínú Bitcoin 1. Èyí mú kí a lè lo Bitcoin fún gbogbo ìwọn owó rírà, pẹ̀lú àwọn iṣòwò kékeré púpọ̀ tó kéré tó senti díẹ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin pín sí 100 mílíọ̀nù sats, èyí jẹ́ kí ó pé fún rírà ti ìwọ̀n èyíkéyìí. Goolu kò lè rọ́rọ̀ pin fún àwọn ìṣòwò kéré.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be moved anywhere in the world instantly over the internet. Real estate is permanently fixed to a specific location and cannot be relocated, making it vulnerable to local economic conditions, natural disasters, and political instability.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin moves anywhere in the world instantly. Real estate is fixed to one location and exposed to local economic, political, and natural risks.
entries.currentValue: A lè gbé Bitcoin lọ sí ibìkìbì lágbáyé lẹ́sẹ̀kẹ̀sẹ̀ lórí intaneti. Ohun-ìní ajé ti di ibì kan pátó a kò sì lè gbé e lọ.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń lọ níbi gbogbo ní àgbáyé lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀. Ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà ti múlẹ̀ ní àyè kan ó sì wà ní ewu àwọn ìṣòro ọrọ̀-ajé, òṣèlú, àti tí ti ara ní àdúgbò.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, making it perfect for transactions of any size. Real estate cannot be easily divided - you can't sell just the kitchen of your house or buy half a bedroom.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats. Real estate can't be partly sold — you can't offload just the kitchen or buy half a bedroom.
entries.currentValue: A lè pín Bitcoin sí èké kékeré miliọ́nù 100 tí a ń pè ní satoshis. A kò lè pín ohun-ìní ajé ní ìrọ̀rùn - o kò lè ta idà kan ilé rẹ níkan.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin pín sí 100 mílíọ̀nù sats. Ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà kò lè jẹ́ títà ní apá — o kò lè ta ile-ìdáná tàbí kí o ra ìdajì yàrá.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network that no government can control. Real estate is subject to extensive government regulation including rent control, eviction moratoriums, zoning laws, and eminent domain where governments can seize your property.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network that no government can control. Real estate is heavily regulated — zoning, rent control, eminent domain, and seizure all apply.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì aláìpín-ààrìn tí ìkálẹ̀ kaǹkaǹ kò lè ṣàkoso. Ohun-ìní ajé wà lábé̀ àwọn ofìn ìkálẹ̀ púpọ̀ pẹ̀lú ìṣàkoso iyalo, eminent domain tí ìkálẹ̀ lè gba ohun-ìní rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì aláìní-àárín tí kò sí ìjọba tí ó lè darí. Ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà ti ní òfin pípọ̀ — ètò agbègbè, dídarí owó iyalo, àṣẹ ìjọba, àti ìgbà-pa wọn gbogbo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin requires no maintenance - it exists as digital code on a network. Real estate requires constant upkeep including repairs, renovations, property management, insurance, and dealing with tenants if rented.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin requires no upkeep. Real estate demands repairs, renovations, insurance, property management, and tenant issues.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin kò nílò ìtòjú - ó wà gégé bí koodu oni-nọ́míbà lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì. Ohun-ìní ajé nílò ìtòjú nígbàgbógbò pẹ̀lú àtúnṣe, àtúnṣẹ, ìṣàkoso ohun-ìní, ìrànsí, àti ṣíṣe pẹ̀lú àwọn iyalo.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò nílò ìtọ́jú. Ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà nílò àwọn àtúnṣe, ìpadàṣe, ìdánilójú, ìṣàkóso ohun-ìní, àti àwọn ìṣòro olùyalo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has no ongoing taxes - you only pay capital gains when you sell. Real estate is subject to annual property taxes that must be paid regardless of whether the property generates income, effectively forcing you to rent your own property from the government forever.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no ongoing taxes — you only pay capital gains when you sell. Real estate owes annual property taxes regardless of income.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin kò ní owó-òyà nígbàgbógbò - o san owó-òyà èré ibi-ówó níkan nígbà tí o bá ta. Ohun-ìní ajé nílò owó-òyà ohun-ìní lóọ̀dún, tó fọ́ kí o san láì ń ṣe àní bóyá ohun-ìní náà máa ń mú owó wá.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò ní owó-ọrẹ tí ń tẹ̀síwájú — o kàn ó sanwó owó èrè bí o bá tà. Ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà ní owó-ọrẹ ohun-ìní ọdọọdún láìka iyè.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin, when backed up properly, cannot be destroyed by floods, fires, earthquakes, hurricanes, or other natural disasters. Real estate is vulnerable to all forms of physical destruction and requires expensive insurance that may not fully cover losses.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin, backed up properly, survives fire, flood, and earthquake. Real estate is vulnerable to every disaster, and insurance rarely covers it all.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin, tí a bá ṣe àfiípamó́ rẹ̀ dáadáa, a kò lè pa run nípà ìkunomi, iná, ìlù, ìjikoko, tàbí àwọn àjálù mìràn. Ohun-ìní ajé wà ní ewu gbogbo irú ìpa run lárà àti pé ó nílò ìrànsí olówó.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin, tí a bá ti dáàbò bo dáadáa, ó là iná, ìkún omi, àti ìmìtìtì ilẹ̀ kọjá. Ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà jẹ́ aláìlágbára sí gbogbo àjálù, ìdánilójú sì sábà ò ní ní bo gbogbo rẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable - one bitcoin equals one bitcoin anywhere in the world. Every piece of real estate is unique with different locations, conditions, and characteristics, making it difficult to price and compare properties.
entries.englishValue: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable. Every property is unique, making pricing and comparisons difficult.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ bakanna àti pé a lè pàṣípààrọ̀ wọn - bitcoin kan dọ́gba bitcoin kan ní ibìkìbì lágbáyé. Ohun-ìní ajé kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ aláìlẹ́gbẹ́ pẹ̀lú àwọn ibì, ipo, àti àwọn àbùdá tó yàtọ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ bákan náà ó sì lè rọ́pò. Ohun-ìní kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ aláìṣe-bákan-náà, èyí ń jẹ́ kí ìpèsè iye àti ìfiwéra ṣòro.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be bought and sold 24/7 by anyone with internet access anywhere in the world. Real estate sales are limited to local buyers, require lengthy processes with lawyers and agents, and can take months to complete.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin trades globally 24/7 by anyone with internet access. Real estate sales are limited to local buyers and can take months of paperwork to close.
entries.currentValue: A lè ra àti ta Bitcoin 24/7 nípà ẹ̀níkaǹkan tó ní iràyè intaneti ní ibìkìbì lágbáyé. Títà ohun-ìní ajé jẹ́ tí àwọn olurà agbègbè, ó nílò ìlànà pipẹ́ pẹ̀lú àwọn agèjà àti àwọn aṣòjú, ó sì lè gba oṣù láti parí.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣòwò ní àgbáyé 24/7 nípasẹ̀ ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó ní ìntánẹ́ẹ̀tì. Títà ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà ní ààlà sí àwọn olùrà àdúgbò ó sì lè gba oṣù ti ìwé-iṣẹ́ láti pari.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin enables direct individual ownership without intermediaries, promoting financial sovereignty for everyone. Buying real estate as an investment beyond your primary residence contributes to the financialization of housing, treating homes as commodities rather than shelter. This drives up prices, reduces affordability for families, and contributes to the housing and homelessness crisis affecting many countries today.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin enables direct individual ownership for anyone. Buying real estate as an investment beyond your primary residence drives up housing prices, reducing affordability and fueling the housing crisis.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin mú níní tààrà ẹ̀níkaǹkan ṣèṣè láì ní alárinà, tó máa ń gbe òmìnìra owó ẹ̀níkaǹkan ga. Rírà ohun-ìní ajé gégé bí idókò kurò nínú ilé àkọ́kó́ rẹ máa ń ṣe kí igbero ilé di ọ̀rọ̀ owó, tó máa ń fa iye ga síì, din ànfààní rírà fún àwọn idílé kù, ó sì máa ń ṣe àjàkálẹ̀ ilé àti aìlẹ́gàn tó ń kàn àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè púpọ̀ lónìí.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ kí ìní tààrà nípa ẹnikẹ́ni ṣeéṣe. Rírà ohun-ìní gbígbé fún ọjà gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìnáwó kọjá ilé pàtàkì rẹ ń sọ iye ilé di gígajù, èyí ń dín àfọwọ́ka kù ó sì ń mú àjálù ilé wá.

entries.englishValueBefore: When you own Bitcoin, you have direct ownership of the asset itself. When you own stocks, you own a share of a company, which means your investment depends on the company's performance, management decisions, and business success.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is a direct asset you own outright. Stocks are shares in a company — their value depends on management, performance, and decisions you can't control.
entries.currentValue: Nígbà tí o bá ní Bitcoin, o ní níní tààrà ọ̀rọ̀ náà funrarẹ. Nígbà tí o bá ní àwọn òhún-ìní, o ní àṣẹ nínú ilé-iṣẹ́, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé idókò rẹ da lórí bí ilé-iṣẹ́ náà ṣe ń ṣe, àwọn ìpinnu aláṣẹ, àti aṣeyori òwò iṣẹ́.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ ohun-ìní tààrà tí o ní pátápátá. Àwọn ọjà jẹ́ ipín ní ilé-iṣẹ́ — iye wọn dá lórí ìṣàkóso, iṣẹ́, àti àwọn ìpinnu tí o kò lè ṣàkóso.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC that will ever exist.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC. Companies can issue new shares at any time, diluting existing shareholders — similar to how fiat
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní opin lílé ti miliọ́nù 21 BTC tí yoo wà láéláé.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ní ààlà tó dúró tí 21 mílíọ̀nù BTC. Àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ lè fún àwọn ipín tuntun ní àkókò èyíkéyìí, èyí ń dín àwọn olùní ipín tí ó wà tẹ́lẹ̀ kù — bákan náà bí

entries.englishValueBefore: Companies can issue new shares at any time, diluting existing shareholders' ownership percentage. This means your slice of the company gets smaller when new shares are created.
entries.englishValue: inflation
entries.currentValue: Àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ lè ṣàjàdé àwọn àṣẹ tuntun ní àkókó kaǹkaǹ, tó máa ń din iye níní àwọn oníàṣẹ tó wà tẹ́lẹ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: owó-ṣíṣẹ́

entries.englishValueBefore: This is less than fiat inflation, but still dilution.
entries.englishValue: dilutes cash. With Bitcoin, your slice never shrinks.
entries.currentValue: Èyí kéré jù owó ṣíṣé fiat, ṣùgbọ́n ó ṣì jẹ́ dídúǹkù.
entries.targetTranslation: fiat ṣe ń dín owó ààmù kù. Pẹ̀lú Bitcoin, apá rẹ kò máa dín kù.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network with no single point of failure. Stock investments are subject to key person risk - if the CEO or other critical leaders leave, get sick, or make poor decisions, your investment can suffer significantly. Companies depend heavily on their leadership teams.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no CEO and no single point of failure. Stocks depend heavily on leadership — one bad decision or departure can tank the price.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì aláìpín-ààrìn láì ní ibì kiko kaǹṣoṣo. Idókò òhún-ìní ní ewu ẹ̀níkan pàtàkì - tí CEO tàbí àwọn olòrí pàtàkì mìràn bá kúrò, ṣàìsàn, tàbí ṣe àwọn ìpinnu tó burú, idókò rẹ lè jìyà púpọ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò ní CEO àti kò ní ojú-ìkùnà kan. Àwọn ọjà dá lórí ìṣàkóso pọ̀ — ìpinnu burúkú kan tàbí ìlọ ẹnìkan lè sọ iye ọjà silẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin's price is determined purely by market supply and demand. Stock prices are often evaluated using P/E ratios (Price-to-Earnings), which show how much investors pay for each dollar of company earnings. High P/E ratios can indicate overvalued stocks, making it harder to determine fair value.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's price comes from open global markets. Stock valuations rely on metrics like P/E ratios that can mask overpriced shares.
entries.currentValue: Iye Bitcoin jẹ́ ìpinù ọ̀jà ìpese àti ìbèèrè níkan. Iye àwọn òhún-ìní máa ń da lórí P/E ratios (Iye-sí-Èré), tó fi hàn méló ni àwọn oludókò san fún dọ́là kọ̀ọ̀kan èré ilé-iṣẹ́. Àwọn P/E ratios tó ga lè tókà pé àwọn òhún-ìní ga jù, tó mú kí ó ṣòro láti mọ̀ iye òtítọ́.
entries.targetTranslation: Iye Bitcoin ti wá láti ọjà àgbáyé tí ó ṣíi sílẹ̀. Ìṣirò ọjà dá lórí àwọn metric bí P/E ratio tí ó lè bo àwọn ipín tí iye wọn pọ̀ jù.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin trades 24 hours a day, 7 days a week on global exchanges.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin trades 24/7 around the world. Stock markets are only open during business hours on weekdays.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ń ṣòwò wàkàtí 24 lójọ́, ọ̀jọ́ 7 lọ́ṣẹ̀ lórí àwọn àyè pàṣípààrọ̀ àgbáyé.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ń ṣòwò 24/7 ní gbogbo àgbáyé. Àwọn ọjà ipín ṣíi nìkan ní àkókò iṣẹ́ ní ọjọ́-ọsẹ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: With Bitcoin, you can take self-custody of your coins, meaning you truly own them without depending on any third party.
entries.englishValue: You can take
entries.currentValue: Pẹ̀lú Bitcoin, o lè gba ìṣàkoso-arà àwọn owó rẹ, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé o ní à ní gídi láì gbékẹ̀lé ẹ̀léekẹ́ta kaǹkaǹ.
entries.targetTranslation: O lè gba

entries.englishValueBefore: Self-custody is as simple as downloading an app.
entries.englishValue: self-custody
entries.currentValue: Ìṣàkoso-arà rọ̀rùn bíí gbàgbé àpù.
entries.targetTranslation: ìṣàkóso-ara

entries.englishValueBefore: Stocks require a brokerage account and you're subject to counterparty risk - if the company goes bankrupt or the brokerage fails, you could lose your investment.
entries.englishValue: of Bitcoin with a simple app — no broker needed. Stocks sit with brokerages, exposing you to counterparty risk if they fail.
entries.currentValue: Àwọn òhún-ìní nílò ààkósílẹ̀ oní-àgbàtẹ àti pé o ní ewu alákóṣẹ́ - tí ilé-iṣẹ́ bá di owó-ajé tàbí oní-àgbàtẹ bá kuna, o lè padánú idókò rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: ti Bitcoin pẹ̀lú app rírọrùn — kò sí alágbàta tí ó nílò. Àwọn ọjà ipín dúró pẹ̀lú àwọn ilé-alágbàta, èyí ń fi ọ́ sínu ewu alábàárìn bí wọ́n bá kùnà.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is a fixed supply asset with a hard cap of 21 million Bitcoin that will ever exist. This makes it a great inflation hedge. Stocks have variable performance against inflation - some companies do well during inflationary periods while others struggle. There's no guarantee that any particular stock will protect against inflation.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's fixed supply makes it a reliable inflation hedge. Some stocks beat inflation, others don't — there's no guarantee.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ ìpese tó wà tèlẹ̀ pẹ̀lú opin lílé ti miliọ́nù 21 Bitcoin tí yoo wà láéláé. Èyí mú kí ó dara gégé bí ààbò owó ṣíṣé. Àwọn òhún-ìní ní iṣẹ́ tó yípadà lòdì sí owó ṣíṣé - àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ kan máa ń ṣe dáadáa nígbà owó ṣíṣé lakoko tí àwọn mìràn máa ń roxò. Kò sí ìdánìléjú pé òhún-ìní kan pàtó yoo dààbò lọ́dì sí owó ṣíṣé.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìpèsè dúró Bitcoin jẹ́ kí ó di àbò gbígbé-pọ̀ owó-ṣíṣẹ́. Diẹ̀ àwọn ọjà ń lu owó-ṣíṣẹ́, díẹ̀ kò ń lu — kò sí ìdánilójú.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is an open network that anyone can join and use without permission. Credit card networks like Visa are closed systems controlled by financial institutions that can deny access to anyone they choose.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is an open network anyone can join and use without permission. Visa is a closed system controlled by financial institutions that can deny access — especially to the unbanked and underbanked.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì gbangba tí ẹ̀níkaǹkan lè dara pọ̀ àti lò láì ní àṣẹ. Àwọn nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì káàdì ifowópàmọ́ bíí Visa jẹ́ ètò tí a tì tí àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ owó ń ṣàkoso tí ó lè kọ à fún ẹ̀níkaǹkan.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì ṣíṣí tí ẹnikẹ́ni lè dara pọ̀ mọ́ ó sì lò láìní ìyọ̀ǹda. Visa jẹ́ ètò pípa tí àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ ìnáwó ti darí, tí ó lè kọ̀ ààyè — pàápàá fún àwọn tí kò ní ilé-ìfowópamọ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin transactions have no fees for merchants, while credit card companies typically charge merchants around 3% per transaction.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin transactions have no merchant fees. Visa typically charges merchants around 3% per transaction — your business can save money accepting
entries.currentValue: Àwọn iṣòwò Bitcoin kò ní owó ìsàn fún àwọn olutà, lakoko tí àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ káàdì ifowópàmọ́ máa ń gba àwọn olutà owó ìsàn 3% fún iṣòwò kọ̀ọ̀kan.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn ìṣòwò Bitcoin kò ní owó alábàwà. Visa sábà ń kó nípa 3% lórí gbogbo ìṣòwò — iṣẹ́ rẹ lè pa owó mọ́ nípa gbígba

entries.englishValueBefore: Learn how your business can save money
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin payments
entries.currentValue: Kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ bí òwò iṣẹ́ rẹ ṣe lè fi owó pamó́
entries.targetTranslation: ìsanwó Bitcoin

entries.englishValueBefore: by accepting Bitcoin payments instead of paying credit card processing fees.
entries.englishValue: instead.
entries.currentValue: nípà gbígbà ìsàn owó Bitcoin dípò sísan owó ìsàn káàdì ifowópàmọ́.
entries.targetTranslation: dípò.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a transparent blockchain where all transactions can be verified by anyone. Credit card networks operate as closed, proprietary systems where transaction details are hidden from public view.
entries.englishValue: Every Bitcoin transaction is on a public, auditable blockchain. Visa runs a closed, proprietary system where customers can't independently verify anything.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ lórí blockchain gbangba tí ẹ̀níkaǹkan lè ṣàyẹ̀wò gbogbo iṣòwò. Àwọn nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì káàdì ifowópàmọ́ máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ gégé bí ètò tí a tì tí àlàyé iṣòwò ì̀kòkò.
entries.targetTranslation: Gbogbo ìṣòwò Bitcoin wà lórí blockchain gbangba tí a lè ṣàyẹ̀wò. Visa ń ṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú ètò pípa ti ara wọn níbi tí àwọn oníbàárà kò ti lè jẹ́rìí sí ohunkóhun lọ́tọ̀.

entries.englishValueBefore: Credit card companies can freeze accounts, block transactions, or deny service at any time. Bitcoin cannot be frozen or controlled by any central authority.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin can't be frozen by any central authority. Visa can freeze accounts, block transactions, or deny service at any time.
entries.currentValue: Àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ káàdì ifowópàmọ́ lè dí ààkósílẹ̀, dá iṣòwò dúró, tàbí kọ láti pèṣè iṣẹ́ ní àkókó kaǹkaǹ. A kò lè dí Bitcoin tàbí ṣàkoso rẹ̀ nípà aláṣẹ ààrìn kaǹkaǹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Kò sí àṣẹ àárín tí ó lè dí Bitcoin. Visa lè dí àwọn àpótí, dí àwọn ìṣòwò, tàbí kí ó kọ̀ ìpèsè ní àkókò èyíkéyìí.

entries.englishValueBefore: Credit cards create debt that can accumulate high interest rates if not paid off quickly, sometimes exceeding 25% annually.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is final-settlement — you can only spend what you own. Credit cards create debt with interest rates often over 25% a year.
entries.currentValue: Káàdì ifowópàmọ́ máa ń ṣẹ̀dá gbèsè tí ó lè kó elè tó ga tí a kò bá san ní kìyà, nígbà mìràn ó lè ju 25% lóọ̀dún.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ ìparí-ìpinnu — o lè ná ohun tí o ní nìkan. Àwọn káàdì kírẹ́dítì ń dá gbèsè pẹ̀lú iye ìfowó-yá tí ó sábà jẹ́ ó ju 25% ní ọdún kan.

entries.englishValueBefore: Accepting Bitcoin has many benefits like accepting payments with lower fees & getting more customers.
entries.englishValue: The simplest way to accept Bitcoin is with a hybrid wallet that automatically sells 100% of the Bitcoin you receive for dollars (or your local currency) the instant a payment comes in.
entries.currentValue: Gbígbà Bitcoin ní ànfààní púpọ̀ bíí gbígbà ìsàn owó pẹ̀lú owó ìsàn tó kéré & gbígbà àwọn oníbàárà díẹ̀ síì.
entries.targetTranslation: Ọ̀nà tí ó rọrùn jùlọ láti gba Bitcoin ni pẹ̀lú àpò àkómọ̀ tí ó ń ta 100% nínú Bitcoin tí o gbà fún dọ́là (tàbí owó àdúgbò rẹ) lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀ tí ìsanwó kan bá dé.

entries.englishValueBefore: If you use a Hybrid Wallet from our Wallet Guide and automatically sell 100% of the Bitcoin you receive for dollars, you don't need to make any changes to your current accounting.
entries.englishValue: With this setup, your books look exactly like they do today — the final number is in dollars, every time. No cost basis, no capital gains, no new spreadsheets.
entries.currentValue: Tí o bá lò Àpò Owó Adàpò láti Àmò̀nà Àpò Owó wa tí o sì ń ta gbogbo Bitcoin tí o gba fún dọ́là láifọ̀wó́yí, o kò nílò láti ṣe ìtẹ̀sí kaǹkan sí ìṣìrò rẹ ló́wó́ló́wó́.
entries.targetTranslation: Pẹ̀lú ètò yìí, ìwé-ìṣirò rẹ máa rí gẹ́gẹ́ bí ó ṣe rí lónìí — iye ìparí náà wà ní dọ́là, ní gbogbo ìgbà. Kò sí ipilẹ̀ owó, kò sí èrè-owó, kò sí ìwé-ìṣirò tuntun.

entries.englishValueBefore: Tracking your cost basis is going to be the biggest difference between accounting for dollars and accounting for Bitcoin. Even if you view your business entirely in terms of Bitcoin, you need to report the dollar value of each transaction on your taxes.
entries.englishValue: Some businesses choose to keep a portion of the Bitcoin they receive instead of auto-converting it all. If that's you, the main extra step is tracking your cost basis — the dollar value of each Bitcoin payment on the day you received it.
entries.currentValue: Ṣíṣe àkósílẹ̀ owó ìpìlẹ̀ṣẹ̀ rẹ ni yoo jẹ́ ìyàtọ̀ tó tóbi jùlọ láàrìn ìṣìrò fún dọ́là àti ìṣìrò fún Bitcoin. Pààpàà tí o bá wo òwò iṣẹ́ rẹ láti ojú Bitcoin níkan, o nílò láti jàbọ́ iye dọ́là iṣòwò kọ̀ọ̀kan lórí owó-òyà rẹ.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn iṣẹ́ kan máa ń yan láti pa apá kan nínú Bitcoin tí wọ́n gbà mọ́ dípò kí wọ́n yí gbogbo rẹ̀ padà. Bí èyí bá rí ọ, ohun pàtàkì tí o ní láti ṣe ni títọpa ipilẹ̀ owó rẹ — iye dọ́là ti ìsanwó Bitcoin kọ̀ọ̀kan ní ọjọ́ tí o gbà á.

entries.englishValueBefore: If you use QuickBooks, you can do this automatically using the Bitcoin Sync plugin.
entries.englishValue: Even if you think of your business entirely in Bitcoin, most tax authorities still want the dollar value reported. The good news: it's just two numbers per transaction — the amount of Bitcoin received and its dollar value on that day.
entries.currentValue: Tí o bá lò QuickBooks, o lè ṣe èyí láifọ̀wó́yí nípà Bitcoin Sync plugin.
entries.targetTranslation: Kódà bí o bá rò pé iṣẹ́ rẹ wà pátápátá ní Bitcoin, ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn aláṣẹ owó-ọrẹ ṣì fẹ́ kí o sọ iye dọ́là. Ìròyìn rere: ó kàn jẹ́ àwọn nọ́mbà méjì lórí ìṣòwò kọ̀ọ̀kan — iye Bitcoin tí a gbà àti iye dọ́là rẹ̀ ní ọjọ́ náà.

entries.englishValueBefore: Inflation happens when more money is printed or created from thin air. This makes your money worth less over time.
entries.englishValue: Inflation happens when more money is printed or created from thin air. That makes the money in your pocket worth less over time — and it's why prices keep going up year after year.
entries.currentValue: Owó ṣíṣé máa ń ṣẹlẹ̀ nígbà tí a bá tẹ̀ owó díẹ̀ síì tàbí ṣẹ̀dá rẹ̀ láti òfé. Èyí mú kí owó rẹ din iye ní pẹ̀lú àkókó.
entries.targetTranslation: Owó-ṣíṣẹ́ máa ń ṣẹlẹ̀ nígbà tí a bá tẹ̀ owó síi tàbí kí a dá a látinú ihò òfo. Èyí ń sọ owó tí ó wà ní àpò rẹ di kéré ní iye pẹ̀lú àkókò — èyí sì ni ìdí tí àwọn iye fi ń ga ní ọdọọdún.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a fixed supply, which means no one can print more Bitcoin.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a fixed supply of 21 million coins. No government, bank, or company can print more of it. Your Bitcoin savings hold their value over time instead of quietly losing it.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ní ìpese tó wà tèlẹ̀, èyí túmọ̀ sí pé kò sí ẹ̀níkan tó lè tẹ̀ Bitcoin díẹ̀ síì.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ní ìpèsè tí ó dúró tí 21 mílíọ̀nù coin. Kò sí ìjọba, ilé-ìfowópamọ́, tàbí ilé-iṣẹ́ tí ó lè tẹ̀ síi. Ìfowópamọ́ Bitcoin rẹ máa di iye rẹ̀ mú lórí àkókò dípò pípàdánù rẹ̀ ní títẹ̀ẹ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Multiple US banks have collapsed in the past few years due to bank runs.
entries.englishValue: Multiple U.S. banks have collapsed in recent years because of bank runs. When too many customers tried to withdraw at once, the banks didn't have the cash to pay everyone back.
entries.currentValue: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ pọ̀ àwọn ilé-ìfòwópàmó́ ní Amẹ́ríkà ti wó ní àwọn ọ̀dún tó ṣàájú kọ̀já nítórí ìjàmbá ilé-ìfòwópàmó́.
entries.targetTranslation: Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ U.S. ti ṣubú ní àwọn ọdún tí ó kọjá nítorí àwọn ìjàmbá ilé-ìfowópamọ́. Nígbà tí àwọn oníbàárà tó pọ̀ jù gbìyànjú láti yọ owó kúrò lẹ́ẹ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan, àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ kò ní owó tó láti sanwó padà sí gbogbo wọn.

entries.englishValueBefore: Instead of just holding your money for you, banks invest and lend out your money. If those investments don't do well, they don't have enough to pay you back.
entries.englishValue: Instead of just holding your money, banks lend and invest most of it. If those investments go bad — or if depositors lose confidence — the bank can fail, and your deposits can be frozen or lost.
entries.currentValue: Dípò kí wọn tọ́jú owó rẹ fún ọ, àwọn ilé-ìfòwópàmó́ máa ń fi owó rẹ ṣòwò àti ya à ní aàwìn. Tí àwọn idókò wọ̀nyí kò bá dára, wọn kò ní owó tó láti san ọ́ padà.
entries.targetTranslation: Dípò kí ó kàn pa owó rẹ mọ́, ilé-ìfowópamọ́ ń yá àti ìnáwó ọ̀pọ̀ rẹ̀. Bí àwọn ìnáwó wọn bá burú jọjọ — tàbí bí àwọn olùpa-mọ́ bá pàdánù ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé — ilé-ìfowópamọ́ lè kùnà, owó rẹ tí o pa mọ́ sì lè jẹ́ dídí tàbí pípàdánù.

entries.englishValueBefore: And the FDIC insurance fund only has $1 for every $100 they're insuring.
entries.englishValue: With Bitcoin, you can hold your own money directly in your own wallet. No bank. No intermediary. No bank run.
entries.currentValue: Àti pé àpàmó́ ìrànsí FDIC ní dọ́là 1 níkan lórí dọ́là 100 kọ̀ọ̀kan tí wọn ń ṣe ìrànsí rẹ̀.
entries.targetTranslation: Pẹ̀lú Bitcoin, o lè di owó tirẹ tààrà nínú àpò tirẹ. Kò sí ilé-ìfowópamọ́. Kò sí alábàárìn. Kò sí ìjàmbá ilé-ìfowópamọ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Unlike traditional financial networks, Bitcoin doesn't require permission to be used.
entries.englishValue: Unlike credit cards, PayPal, or traditional bank accounts, Bitcoin doesn't require anyone's permission to use.
entries.currentValue: Kò dàbí àwọn nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì owó ìṣààjú, Bitcoin kò nílò àṣẹ kí o tó lò.
entries.targetTranslation: Yàtọ̀ sí àwọn káàdì kírẹ́dítì, PayPal, tàbí àwọn àpótí ilé-ìfowópamọ́ ìbílẹ̀, Bitcoin kò nílò ìyọ̀ǹda ẹnikẹ́ni láti lò.

entries.englishValueBefore: That means no one can stop you from using Bitcoin for any reason. It's the first financial network you can use without fear of censorship or seizure.
entries.englishValue: No one can freeze your account, block a payment, or cut you off from the network. It's the first financial system in history you can use freely, without fear of censorship or seizure.
entries.currentValue: Èyí túmọ̀ sí pé kò sí ẹ̀níkan tó lè da ọ́ dúró láti lo Bitcoin fún ìdjú kaǹkaǹ. Ó jẹ́ nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì owó àkọ́kó́ tí o lè lò láì bẹ̀rù fún ìṣàkoso tàbí gbage.
entries.targetTranslation: Kò sí ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó lè dí àpótí rẹ, dí ìsanwó kan, tàbí kí ó gé ọ kúrò ní nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì. Ó jẹ́ ètò ìnáwó àkọ́kọ́ nínú ìtàn tí o lè lò ní òmìnira, láìbẹ̀rù àdílọ́lẹ́ tàbí ìgbà-pa.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is a misunderstood technology that is building a better world.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is often misunderstood, but it's quietly doing a lot of good in the world.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin jẹ́ ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ̀ tí a kò lóyé tó ń kó̀ àgbáyé tó dára jùlọ.
entries.targetTranslation: A sábà ń ṣe àìlóye Bitcoin, ṣùgbọ́n ó ń ṣe rere púpọ̀ ní àgbáyé ní ìpalọ́lọ́.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has enabled human rights activists to fight for freedom, reduced global methane emissions, saved national parks, and so much more.
entries.englishValue: It has helped human rights activists fight for freedom, reduced global methane emissions from landfills and oil fields, stabilized electric grids, and funded public goods like national parks.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ti mú kí àwọn olùgbàlà ẹ̀tọ́ òmònìyàn lè jà fún òmìnìra, din itusilẹ̀ methane ní àgbáyé, gba àwọn ọ̀gán orílẹ̀-èdè là, àti òpọ̀lọ pọ̀ mìràn.
entries.targetTranslation: Ó ti ràn àwọn alágbàwí ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn lọ́wọ́ láti jagun fún òmìnira, dín ìjáde gáàsì methane àgbáyé kù láti àwọn pápá ìjẹjù àti àwọn pápá epo, mú àwọn nẹ́tíwọ́ọ̀kì iná dúró sín, ó sì pèsè owó fún àwọn ohun-èlò gbangba bí àwọn ọgbà ìṣẹ̀dáyé orílẹ̀-èdè.

entries.targetTranslation: ní 2022 pẹ̀lú ètò rírọrùn: yára ìgbàfẹ́ Bitcoin nípasẹ̀ ẹ̀kọ́.

entries.englishValue: We mail free Bitcoin stickers to your door so you can help spread Bitcoin awareness in your community. Hundreds of people scan the QR codes on these stickers each month to learn about Bitcoin.
entries.targetTranslation: A fi àwọn àlèmọ́ Bitcoin ọ̀fẹ́ ránṣẹ́ sí ẹnu-ọ̀nà rẹ kí o lè ràn lọ́wọ́ láti tan ìmọ̀ Bitcoin kálẹ̀ ní àyíká rẹ. Àwọn ọgọrùn-ún ènìyàn ń wo àwọn QR code lórí àwọn àlèmọ́ wọ̀nyí lóṣooṣù láti kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa Bitcoin.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin doesn't have bank runs
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin kò ní ìjàmbá ilé-ìfowópamọ́

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is a full-reserve system. You're not depositing your money in a bank. You are your own bank. There's no lending out your money without your knowledge because you are the only one who can access your money.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin jẹ́ ètò ìpamọ́-pípé. O kò pa owó rẹ mọ́ ní ilé-ìfowópamọ́. Ìwọ ni ilé-ìfowópamọ́ ara rẹ. Kò sí àyà owó rẹ láìmọ̀ọ́mọ̀ nítorí ìwọ nìkan ni ó lè wọ owó rẹ.

entries.englishValue: As long as you hold bitcoin in your own wallet — not on an exchange or wrapped in an ETF — bank runs are impossible.
entries.targetTranslation: Niwọ̀n ìgbà tí o bá di Bitcoin nínú àpò tirẹ — kì í ṣe lórí ọjà tàbí nínú ETF — àwọn ìjàmbá ilé-ìfowópamọ́ kò ṣeéṣe.

entries.englishValue: With Bitcoin, you're truly in control of your money.
entries.targetTranslation: Pẹ̀lú Bitcoin, o ní ìṣàkóso lóòótọ́ lórí owó rẹ.

entries.englishValue: Since March 26, 2020, U.S. banks are required to hold 0% in reserves.
entries.targetTranslation: Látinú Oṣù Kẹta 26, 2020, àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ U.S. ní láti pa 0% mọ́ ní ìpamọ́.

entries.englishValue: FDIC insurance covers about 1% of deposits
entries.targetTranslation: Ìdánilójú FDIC ń bo nípa 1% nínú àwọn ìpamọ́

entries.englishValue: FDIC insurance protects deposits up to $250,000 per depositor. But the insurance fund is tiny compared to the total deposits it's supposed to protect.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìdánilójú FDIC ń dáàbò bo àwọn ìpamọ́ títí $250,000 fún olùpa-mọ́ kọ̀ọ̀kan. Ṣùgbọ́n owó ìdánilójú náà kéré gan-an ní ìfiwéra pẹ̀lú àpapọ̀ àwọn ìpamọ́ tí ó yẹ kí ó dáàbò.

entries.englishValue: In a large-scale bank failure, the government would likely print money to cover the gap — resulting in more
entries.targetTranslation: Nínú ìkùnà ilé-ìfowópamọ́ tí ó tóbi, ìjọba lè tẹ̀ owó láti bo ààlà náà — èyí yóò yọrí sí

entries.englishValue: inflation.
entries.targetTranslation: owó-ṣíṣẹ́ síi.

entries.englishValue: Banks lend out your deposits under fractional reserve banking. If too many people withdraw at once, banks can fail. Bitcoin is a full-reserve system — bank runs are impossible.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ ń yá àwọn ìpamọ́ rẹ kúrò lábẹ́ ètò ìpamọ́-ọ̀wọ̀n. Bí àwọn ènìyàn tó pọ̀ jù bá yọ owó kúrò lẹ́ẹ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan, àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ lè kùnà. Bitcoin jẹ́ ètò ìpamọ́-pípé — àwọn ìjàmbá ilé-ìfowópamọ́ kò ṣeéṣe.

entries.englishValue: Silicon Valley Bank: a real example
entries.targetTranslation: Silicon Valley Bank: àpẹẹrẹ gidi

entries.englishValue: In March 2023, Silicon Valley Bank failed after investing customer deposits in long-term
entries.targetTranslation: Ní Oṣù Kẹta 2023, Silicon Valley Bank kùnà lẹ́yìn tí ó ti ná àwọn ìpamọ́ oníbàárà sínú ọ̀rọ̀ ìdúró-pẹ́

entries.englishValue: When those bonds lost value, SVB couldn't cover withdrawals. The bank was insolvent.
entries.targetTranslation: Nígbà tí àwọn ìfòwó-mu wọ̀nyẹn pàdánù iye, SVB kò lè bo àwọn àyà. Ilé-ìfowópamọ́ náà kò ní owó.

entries.englishValue: government bonds.
entries.targetTranslation: ìfòwó-mu ìjọba.

entries.englishValue: Thousands of businesses couldn't pay their employees. The FDIC stepped in — but that raised a bigger question: is your money actually safe?
entries.targetTranslation: Ẹgbẹẹgbẹ̀rún àwọn iṣẹ́ kò lè san àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ wọn. FDIC wọ inú rẹ̀ — ṣùgbọ́n èyí gbé ìbéèrè ńlá: ṣé owó rẹ wà ní àìséwu lóòótọ́?

entries.englishValue: Banks don't hold your deposits in a vault. They lend your money out and invest it — that's called fractional reserve banking.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ kò ní àwọn ìpamọ́ rẹ nínú àpò-ìpamọ́. Wọ́n ń yá owó rẹ kúrò wọ́n sì ń ná a — èyí ni a pè ní ètò ìpamọ́-ọ̀wọ̀n.

entries.englishValue: If too many people try to withdraw at the same time, the bank doesn't have enough cash to pay everyone. That's a bank run — and it can cause banks to collapse entirely.
entries.targetTranslation: Bí àwọn ènìyàn tó pọ̀ jù bá gbìyànjú láti yọ kúrò lẹ́ẹ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan, ilé-ìfowópamọ́ kò ní owó tó láti sanwó padà sí gbogbo wọn. Èyí ni ìjàmbá ilé-ìfowópamọ́ — ó sì lè mú kí àwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ ṣubú pátápátá.

entries.englishValue: Accepting Bitcoin at your business doesn't have to complicate your accounting. Here's the short version — plus the tools and pros to make it painless.
entries.targetTranslation: Gbígba Bitcoin ní iṣẹ́ rẹ kò ní láti díjú ìṣirò rẹ. Èyí ni ẹ̀dà kúkúrú — pẹ̀lú àwọn ohun-èlò àti àwọn akọṣẹ́mọṣẹ́ láti ṣe é láìṣòro.

entries.englishValue: If you already accept cash or card, adding Bitcoin to your business books is simpler than it looks. You have two paths: auto-convert every Bitcoin payment to dollars the moment it arrives (no new accounting needed), or keep some as Bitcoin (a few extra numbers to track).
entries.targetTranslation: Bí o bá ti ń gba owó ààmù tàbí káàdì, fífi Bitcoin kún ìwé-ìṣirò iṣẹ́ rẹ rọrùn ju bí ó ti rí. O ní ọ̀nà méjì: yí gbogbo ìsanwó Bitcoin padà sí dọ́là lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀ tí ó dé (kò sí ìṣirò tuntun tí ó nílò), tàbí kí o pa apá kan mọ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí Bitcoin (àwọn nọ́mbà afikún díẹ̀ láti tọpa).

entries.englishValue: This guide walks you through both — so you can pick the one that fits your business and start accepting Bitcoin with confidence.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìtọ́sọ́nà yìí gbà ọ kọjá àwọn méjèèjì — kí o lè yan ọ̀kan tí ó bá iṣẹ́ rẹ mu kí o sì bẹ̀rẹ̀ gbígba Bitcoin ní ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé.

entries.englishValue: The easy path: auto-convert to dollars
entries.targetTranslation: Ọ̀nà rírọrùn: yí padà sí dọ́là láìjáde

entries.englishValue: That's it. The underlying math is identical to how any other appreciating or depreciating asset is accounted for.
entries.targetTranslation: Ìyẹn nìkan ni. Ìṣirò abẹ́nú jẹ́ ó dúró pẹ̀lú bí a ṣe ń ṣe iṣirò ohun-ìní mìíràn tí ó ń pọ̀ tàbí dín kù.

entries.englishValue: Tap any question below to expand the answer. When you're ready to start accepting Bitcoin, the business resources at the bottom of the page will walk you through each step.

entries.englishValue: Accept Bitcoin at your business for lower fees, instant settlement, no chargebacks, and more customers.
entries.targetTranslation: Gba Bitcoin ní iṣẹ́ rẹ fún owó kéré, ìparí lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀, kò sí àwọn chargeback, àti àwọn oníbàárà síi.

entries.englishValue: Accept payments with lower fees, get paid instantly, and reach millions of new customers — with zero contracts and zero hidden costs.
entries.targetTranslation: Gba àwọn ìsanwó pẹ̀lú owó kéré, gba ìsanwó lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀, kí o sì dé àwọn mílíọ̀nù àwọn oníbàárà tuntun — pẹ̀lú odò àdéhùn àti odò àwọn iye tí ó pamọ́.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin gives your business a faster, cheaper, more private way to get paid. No middlemen. No chargebacks. No contracts. Just money that settles in seconds, directly from your customers to you.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin fún iṣẹ́ rẹ ní ọ̀nà tí ó yára, olówó-pọ́ọ́kú, àti àdáni síi láti gba ìsanwó. Kò sí àwọn alábàárìn. Kò sí àwọn chargeback. Kò sí àwọn àdéhùn. Kàn owó tí ó pari ní àwọn ìṣẹ́jú díẹ̀, tààrà láti àwọn oníbàárà rẹ sí ọ.

entries.englishValue: Below is the short version of why Bitcoin is good for business — and below that, every resource you need to start accepting it today.
entries.targetTranslation: Nísàlẹ̀ ni ẹ̀dà kúkúrú ti ìdí tí Bitcoin fi dára fún iṣẹ́ — àti nísàlẹ̀ ni gbogbo ohun-èlò tí o nílò láti bẹ̀rẹ̀ gbígba lónìí.

entries.englishValue: List your business for free on BTC Map — the open, worldwide directory of Bitcoin-accepting merchants — so Bitcoiners nearby can find you and spend Bitcoin at your business.
entries.targetTranslation: Fi iṣẹ́ rẹ pamọ́ ní ọ̀fẹ́ lórí BTC Map — atọ́nà àgbáyé ṣíṣí ti àwọn alágbatà tí ó gba Bitcoin — kí àwọn Bitcoiner tí ó súnmọ́ rẹ lè rí ọ kí wọ́n sì ná Bitcoin ní iṣẹ́ rẹ.

entries.englishValue: Get your business on Bitcoin merchant maps

entries.englishValue: Bitcoiners actively look for places to spend. Getting your business on the map puts you in front of every Bitcoin user searching for somewhere to eat, shop, or stay nearby — at zero cost to you.
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn Bitcoiner ń wá àwọn ibi láti ná lóòótọ́. Fífi iṣẹ́ rẹ sórí map fi ọ́ síwájú gbogbo olùmúlò Bitcoin tí ó ń wá ibi láti jẹun, ra, tàbí dúró sí — ní odò iye fún ọ.

entries.englishValue: Just fill out the short form below and we'll submit your business to BTC Map and other Bitcoin merchant maps for you.
entries.targetTranslation: Kàn kún fọ́mù kúkúrú nísàlẹ̀, a ó sì fi iṣẹ́ rẹ ránṣẹ́ sí BTC Map àti àwọn map alágbatà Bitcoin mìíràn fún ọ.

entries.englishValue: We'll create and publish your sticker files within 3 to 4 weeks. Once they're ready, you'll be able to download and print them for free from our sticker files page.
entries.targetTranslation: A ó dá àwọn àkójọpọ̀ àlèmọ́ rẹ kí a sì tẹ̀ wọ́n jáde láàárín ọ̀sẹ̀ 3 sí 4. Lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá ti ṣetán, ìwọ ó lè ṣe ìgbàsílẹ̀ wọn láti ojú-ìwé àkójọpọ̀ àlèmọ́ wa kí o sì tẹ̀ wọ́n ní ọ̀fẹ́.

entries.englishValue: Sticker files are released in batches, so it may take a few weeks for your language to go live. Thanks for your patience!
entries.targetTranslation: A tu àwọn àkójọpọ̀ àlèmọ́ jáde ní àwọn ìpín, nítorí náà ó lè gba ọ̀sẹ̀ díẹ̀ fún èdè rẹ láti wà lórí ojú-ìwé. O ṣé fún sùúrù rẹ!

entries.englishValue: Free 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' stickers
entries.targetTranslation: Àwọn àlèmọ́ 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' ọ̀fẹ́

entries.englishValue: Accepting Bitcoin is only half the job — your customers also need to know that you do. These small 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' stickers are designed to stick on your front door, register, menu, or anywhere else customers will see them before they pay.
entries.targetTranslation: Gbígba Bitcoin jẹ́ ìdajì iṣẹ́ nìkan — àwọn oníbàárà rẹ pẹ̀lú nílò láti mọ̀ pé o ṣe é. Àwọn àlèmọ́ kéré 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' wọ̀nyí ni a ṣe láti so mọ́ ẹnu-ọ̀nà iwájú rẹ, olùgbasilẹ, menu, tàbí ibi mìíràn tí àwọn oníbàárà yóò rí i kí wọ́n tó sanwó.
